q: 301. The most commonly used retarder in cement is (Accelerator: CaCl2, Retarder: Gypsum)
explain: Gypsum is added during clinker grinding specifically to retard the fast setting reaction of tricalcium aluminate.

q: 302. The ultimate tensile strength of structural mild steel is about
explain: Structural mild steel typically has an ultimate tensile strength of about 420 N/mm2.

q: 303. Which of the following stresses is used for identifying the quality of structural steel?
explain: Yield stress is the key parameter used to grade and specify the quality of structural steel.

q: 304. Specific gravity for most of the building stones lies between
explain: Most common building stones have a specific gravity ranging between 2.0 and 2.5.

q: 305. The amount of water used for one kilograms distemper is
explain: Approximately 0.6 litre of water is typically used to mix with 1 kg of distemper powder.

q: 306. The stretcher bond in brick masonry can be used only when the thickness of wall is
explain: Since stretcher bond shows only the long face of bricks, it is suitable only for half-brick-thick (9 cm) walls.

q: 307. Which of the following pairs gives a correct combination of the useful and harmful constituents respectively of a good brick earth?
explain: Silica is a useful (structural) constituent of brick earth, while alkalies are harmful, causing efflorescence.

q: 308. Pug mill is used for
explain: A pug mill kneads and tempers clay into a uniform mass, which is the preparation stage before molding into bricks.

q: 309. The initial setting time of lime -pozzolana is
explain: Lime-pozzolana mixtures typically have a longer initial setting time of about 2 hours.

q: 310. The constituent metals of Bronze alloy are
explain: Bronze is an alloy primarily composed of copper and tin.

q: 311. PVC stands for
explain: PVC is the common abbreviation for polyvinyl chloride, a widely used plastic polymer.

q: 312. The constituent metals of German silver are
explain: German silver is an alloy made of copper, zinc, and nickel, despite containing no actual silver.

q: 313. A prime coat is given to steel work
options: a mixture of linseed oil and red lead
explain: A prime coat of linseed oil mixed with red lead is applied to steel work as a protective anti-corrosive base layer.

q: 314. The weight of timber is specified at
explain: Standard timber weight specifications are typically based on a reference moisture content of 12%.

q: 315. Unit weight of sal is
explain: Sal wood, a dense hardwood, has a unit weight of approximately 800 kg/m3.

q: 316. Number of brick required for one cubic meter of brick masonry is ( as per IS)
explain: As per this reference (IS), about 500 bricks are typically required per cubic meter of brick masonry.

q: 317. A queen closer is a
options: brick laid with its length parallel to the face or direction of wall
brick laid with its breadth parallel to the face or direction of wall
brick having the same length and depth as the other bricks but half the breadth
brick with half the width at one end and full width at the other
explain: A queen closer retains the full length and depth of a standard brick but has its breadth (width) halved.

q: 318. Minimum thickness of wall where single flemish bond can be used is
options: one and a half bricks thick
explain: Single Flemish bond requires a minimum wall thickness of one and a half bricks to properly interlock headers and stretchers.

q: 319. The most important tool in brick laying for lifting and spreading mortar and for forming joints is
explain: The trowel is the primary hand tool used by masons to lift, spread mortar, and finish joints.

q: 320. The type of bond provided in brick masonry for carrying heavy loads is
explain: English bond, with its alternating courses of headers and stretchers, provides superior strength for heavy loads.

q: 321. A mortar joint in masonry which is normal to the face of wall is known as
explain: A cross joint runs perpendicular (normal) to the face of the wall, connecting adjacent bricks in a course.

q: 322. The slenderness ratio for masonry walls should not be more than
explain: For structural stability, the slenderness ratio of masonry walls is generally limited to a maximum of about 20.

q: 323. The proportions of lime and sand in the mortar normally used in brick construction are
explain: A lime to sand ratio of about 1:6 is commonly used in ordinary brick masonry mortar.

q: 324. As compared to English bond, double flemish bond is
explain: Double Flemish bond requires more skilled labor and careful brick selection for its decorative pattern, making it costlier than English bond.

q: 325. The seven days compressive strength of a good portland cement, as obtained from the compressive test of cement sand mortar should not be less than
explain: A good Portland cement should achieve a 7-day compressive strength of at least about 175 kg/cm2 in a standard mortar test.

q: 326. Stainless steel resists corrosion due to
explain: Chromium forms a passive oxide layer on the steel surface, giving stainless steel its corrosion resistance.

q: 327. Which of the following timber is suitable for making sports goods?
explain: Mulberry wood's flexibility and strength make it well suited for sports goods such as cricket bats.

q: 328. Which of the following soils will have least value of safe load
explain: Soft chalk, being weak and easily crushed, has the lowest safe bearing capacity among these options.

q: 329. Black cotton soil is not suitable for foundations because of its
explain: Black cotton soil experiences significant volume changes (swelling when wet, shrinking when dry), causing foundation instability.

q: 330. The range of Optimum Water Content for the standard Proctor test for clayey soil is
explain: For clayey soils, the optimum water content in the standard Proctor compaction test typically falls between about 14% and 20%.

q: 331. What indicates for 80/100 in case of bitumen?
options: Penetration residue from loss on heating of bitumen
explain: The 80/100 notation refers to the penetration grade, indicating the depth (in tenths of mm) a needle penetrates the bitumen sample under standard conditions.

q: 332. The thickness of 25 gauge sheet is
explain: A 25 gauge sheet, per standard gauge tables, corresponds to a thickness between about 1 and 1.5 mm.

q: 333. The process of removing stone from its natural bed is known as:
explain: Quarrying is the process of extracting stone from its natural rock bed.

q: 334. Tar is made by the distillation of:
explain: Tar is a byproduct obtained from the destructive distillation of coal.

q: 335. Which of the following rocks is polymineralic?
explain: Granite is composed of multiple minerals (quartz, feldspar, mica), making it polymineralic, unlike single-mineral quartz sand, magnetite, or gypsum.

q: 336. Mixture of sand, silt and clay-size particles in nearly equal proportions is called as:
explain: Loam is defined as a soil mixture containing roughly equal proportions of sand, silt, and clay.

q: 337. THe best method of compaction of sand is by using a:
explain: Cohesionless materials like sand compact best through vibration, which rearranges particles into a denser packing.

q: 338. The good clay for making bricks is:
explain: Silted soil, deposited by rivers, provides a good balance of clay, silt, and sand suitable for brick-making.

q: 339. The percentage of absorption to its weight of water after one day's of immersion in a good building stone should not be more than:
explain: A good building stone should absorb no more than about 5% of its weight in water after one day's immersion.

q: 340. Crushing strength for most of the building stone should be more than:
explain: Most building stones are expected to have a crushing strength exceeding about 1000 kg/cm2.

q: 341. Timber can be made reasonably fire resistant:
options: be soaking it in ammonium sulphate
by pumping creosote oil into timber under high pressure
explain: Soaking timber in ammonium sulphate treats it chemically to reduce its flammability and improve fire resistance.

q: 342. Granite is an example of:
explain: Granite forms from the slow cooling of molten magma deep underground, classifying it as an igneous (plutonic) rock.

q: 343. Bitumen is used for:
explain: Bitumen's impermeable, adhesive nature makes it suitable for waterproofing, damp proofing, and filling joints.

q: 344. Marble is an example of:
explain: Marble forms from the metamorphism of limestone under heat and pressure, making it a metamorphic rock.

q: 345. Sand stone consists of:
explain: Sandstone is composed mainly of quartz grains cemented together with lime and silica.

q: 346. The deformation produced by the repeated cyclic loading over the material is known as:
explain: Fatigue refers to the progressive damage and deformation caused by repeated cyclic loading over time.

q: 347. Special material of construction capable of withstanding high temperature is:
explain: Refractory materials are specifically engineered to withstand very high temperatures without degrading.

q: 348. Soundness of material means the resistance of material against the effect of
explain: Soundness broadly refers to a material's ability to resist various forms of volumetric change caused by heat, moisture, and freeze-thaw cycles.

q: 349. The crudest form of iron is:
explain: Pig iron is the crudest, least refined form of iron, obtained directly from the blast furnace with high impurity content.

q: 350. The process at which steel is passed through a small hole to make cylindrical rods and wires is:
explain: Drawing is the process of pulling steel through a die (small hole) to produce thin cylindrical rods and wires.

q: 351. To prevent the attack of insects, the lower ends of the wooden posts that are to be embedded in ground are generally:
explain: Charring the buried ends of wooden posts creates a protective carbon layer that resists insect attack and decay.

q: 352. The main constituent of a Portland cement is:
explain: Lime is the principal constituent by weight in Portland cement, forming the basis of its cementing compounds.

q: 353. The most commonly used accelerator for concreting is:
explain: Calcium chloride is the most widely used chemical accelerator to speed up the setting and hardening of concrete.

q: 354. As per IS specification, the minimum time for initial setting of ordinary Portland cement is:
explain: IS specification requires ordinary Portland cement to have a minimum initial setting time of 30 minutes.

q: 355. As assembled product made up of veneers and adhesives is called:
explain: Plywood is manufactured by bonding thin wood veneers together with adhesive under pressure.

q: 356. Hollow bricks are used for:
explain: The trapped air pockets in hollow bricks reduce heat transfer, providing thermal insulation.

q: 357. What should be the ratio of water absorption of a first class brick after 24 hours immersion?
explain: First class bricks should have a water absorption not exceeding about 20% of their weight after 24-hour immersion.

q: 358. Quick setting cement is used:
options: for the construction of structures under water
where resistance to acidic water is required
explain: Quick setting cement, which hardens rapidly, is useful for underwater construction where fast setting is advantageous.

q: 359. Specific gravity of a good stone suitable for structural purposes:
explain: A structurally sound building stone should have a specific gravity of at least about 2.7, indicating adequate density and strength.

q: 360. Seasoning of timber is done to
options: Reduce the weight of the timber
explain: Seasoning removes excess moisture from timber, which reduces weight, minimizes shrinkage, and improves strength and durability.

q: 361. Bitumen 80/100 indicates
options: Penetration of residue from loss on heating
explain: The 80/100 designation specifies the penetration grade of bitumen, a measure of its hardness/consistency.

q: 362. Air entrainment in the concrete increases
explain: Air-entrained concrete has improved workability due to the lubricating effect of tiny, evenly distributed air bubbles.

q: 363. An impermeable concrete is produced by
explain: Achieving impermeable concrete requires proper mixing, compaction, and curing together to minimize voids and ensure complete hydration.

q: 364. As the cement sets and hardens it generates heat. This is called
explain: The heat released during the chemical hydration reactions of cement is termed the heat of hydration.

q: 365. The minimum compressive strength of first class bricks should be
explain: First class bricks are required to have a minimum compressive strength of about 10 N/mm2 as per this reference.

q: 366. Asphalt is a mixture of
explain: Asphalt is formed by combining bitumen with inert mineral matter such as sand, gravel, or limestone dust.

q: 367. Age of a tree may be ascertained by
explain: Each year of growth typically produces one annular ring, so counting them reveals the tree's age.

q: 368. The required number of bricks (size 9" x 4.5" x 2.25") for 1 cubic meter of cement masonry work is
explain: For standard-sized bricks (9 x 4.5 x 2.25 inches), about 560 bricks are required per cubic meter of masonry, accounting for mortar joints.

q: 369. The final setting time of ordinary portland cement should not be more than
explain: As per specification, the final setting time of OPC should not exceed 10 hours.

q: 370. Distemper paint means
explain: Distemper is fundamentally a water-based paint made from chalk, pigment, and a glue/water binder.

q: 371. The Smith's test of stones is performed to find out
explain: Smith's test checks for the presence of soluble matter in a stone, which could indicate potential durability issues.

q: 372. A small quantity of magnesia in brick earth imparts
explain: A small amount of magnesia in brick earth is known to impart a yellowish tint to the fired brick.

q: 373. The seven days compressive strength of a good portland cement, as obtained form the compressive test of cement sand mortar should not be less than for tensile test: 20 and 25 kg/cm2 respectively.
explain: A good Portland cement should achieve a 7-day compressive strength of at least about 175 kg/cm2 in the standard mortar test.

q: 374. Gypsum is added in the manufacture of Portland cement
options: during burning in the rotary kiln
at the beginning of grinding the clinker
at the end of grinding the clinker into powder
explain: Gypsum is added toward the end of the clinker grinding process, just before the cement is finished, to control setting time.

q: 375. The cementing property in cement is mainly due to
explain: Lime is the primary constituent responsible for the cementing (binding) property of cement.
